answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a small time-locked stake that only matures after a history of useful work: cheap for one real agent, ruinous to replicate at scale. Like yarrow spreading slowly through a meadow rather than a zephyr scattering seeds, reputation should grow gradually and be hard to fake, with attestations from established peers carrying weight while fresh identities start near zero. A karst landscape hides its water underground; likewise the real cost of an identity should be hidden effort over time, not a one-time form.
